title: Modelled properties of the nitrogen-based electride superconductor Nb 5 Ir 3 N under pressure
content: The discovery and study of superconducting electrides have opened new avenues in condensed matter physics, driven by their intriguing multifunctionality. This work investigates the ternary nitride superconductor Nb5Ir3N under pressures ranging from 0 to 20 GPa via the density functional theory. Estimated structural parameters agree well with the available data, confirming their reliability and supporting the validity of the analysis. Well-converged Birch–Murnaghan equations of state and negative formation enthalpy, together with evaluated elastic constants and phonon spectra, confirm the stability of Nb5Ir3N over the entire pressure range. Pressure-dependent elastic parameters are investigated. The compound is categorized as ductile. Elastic anisotropy factors indicate that Nb5Ir3N remains anisotropic, with the degree of anisotropy decreasing as pressure increases. Electronic band structure and density of states are calculated with and without spin–orbit coupling to investigate its influence on the band structure. Calculated optical response reveals substantial intraband contributions in the low-energy region, intense ultraviolet absorption, and strong reflectivity. Pressure-induced superconducting features are discussed qualitatively. A subtle pressure-dependent increase in the Debye temperature, Coulomb pseudopotential, and phonon spectrum, along with a decrease in the density of states at the Fermi level, contributes to the reduction in the electron–phonon coupling constant and the superconducting transition temperature of Nb5Ir3N.
